name: Developer Volume Mixing Calculator
description: Calculate exact proportions of two developers (10, 20, 30, 40 Vol) to hit any custom target volume in ml or fluid ounces.
intro: When you run low on 20 Volume developer behind the chair, you don't need to cancel your client. Using Pearson's alligation formula, this calculator tells you the exact ratio of 10 Vol and 30 Vol (or 10 Vol and 40 Vol) to blend for an exact target strength with zero chemical guesswork.
formula_summary: Formula: Parts Low = High Vol - Target Vol | Parts High = Target Vol - Low Vol. Mix in digital grams or fluid ounces.

name: Bleach & Lightener Ratio Calculator
description: Tare your digital scale and calculate exact gram weights for 1:1, 1:1.5, 1:2, and 1:3 powder lightener ratios.
intro: Consistency is everything in blonding. Whether you need a thick 1:1 clay consistency for open-air balayage or a smooth 1:2 foil ratio, this tool gives you precise gram and ounce measurements to prevent over-dilution and bowl waste.
formula_summary: Formula: Developer Weight = Powder Grams × Ratio Multiplier (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, or 3.0). Total Bowl Weight = Powder + Developer.

name: Hair Level & Undertone Neutralizer Guide
description: Identify exposed warmth at levels 1 through 10 and look up the exact counteracting toner pigments on the color wheel.
intro: Every level of lift exposes a predictable underlying pigment—from red at Level 2 up to pale yellow at Level 9. Use this interactive chart to instantly identify the exact complementary pigment required to neutralize brassiness or enhance golden tones.
formula_summary: Color Wheel Rule: Green neutralizes Red (Levels 1–3), Blue neutralizes Orange (Levels 5–6), Violet neutralizes Yellow (Levels 8–10).

name: Grey Hair Coverage Formulation Calculator
description: Formulate exact base-to-fashion shade ratios based on client grey percentage (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%).
intro: Translucent grey hair lacks natural background pigment. To achieve 100% opaque coverage on stubborn grey hair, you must blend a dedicated Natural/Base series with your client's target fashion shade. This calculator provides the exact gram breakdown.
formula_summary: Standard Formulation: 25% grey = 25% Natural Base | 50% grey = 50% Natural Base | 75%+ grey = 66%–75% Natural Base with 20 Vol developer.

name: Balayage Service Cost & Product Estimator
description: Calculate backbar product costs, toner bowls, bond builders, and labor time to quote profitable balayage services.
intro: Balayage is one of the highest-revenue salon services, but extra bowls of clay lightener, glosses, and bond builders can quickly destroy your profit margins if not calculated. Use this tool to quote transparent, profitable blonding appointments.
formula_summary: Service Quote Formula: (Lightener Bowls × Cost) + (Gloss Bowls × Cost) + Bond Builder + (Service Hours × Target Hourly Rate).

name: Hair Toner Ratio & Processing Timer
description: Calculate demi-permanent gloss ratios (1:1 vs 1:2) and optimal processing times for damp or dry toning.
intro: Toning damp hair provides sheer, translucent results, while dry application yields maximum depth and longevity. This calculator gives you exact liquid gloss to dedicated processing lotion proportions.
formula_summary: Standard Liquid Gloss Ratio: 1 part toner to 1 or 2 parts dedicated developer (5–10 Vol). Visual check every 5 minutes up to 20 minutes.

name: Color Correction Time & Quote Estimator
description: Estimate realistic appointment hours, color remover steps, and hourly pricing for multi-stage corrective color.
intro: Color corrections are unpredictable. Charging a flat rate often results in working for below minimum wage. This calculator breaks down color extraction, test strands, re-pigmentation, and glossing into transparent hourly blocks.
formula_summary: Color Correction Quote: Total Stages (Decap / Fill / Foil / Gloss) × 1.25 Hours/Stage × Hourly Rate + Backbar Buffer.
keywords: how to charge for color correction

name: Foil Usage & Placement Calculator
description: Calculate exact foil count, weave vs slice density, and box usage for full head, partial, and money piece services.
intro: Eliminate pre-cut foil waste and streamline your setup. Estimate exact foil requirements for standard partials (30–45 foils) up to maximum-density platinum card sessions (120+ foils).
formula_summary: Foil Guidelines: Money Piece (8–12 foils), Partial (35–50 foils), Full Head (70–90 foils), Platinum Card (110–140 foils).
keywords: how many foils for full head

name: Perm Rod Size & Curl Diameter Guide
description: Determine perm rod diameter (red, yellow, blue, white, purple) to match client target wave or curl pattern.
intro: Perm rod selection determines the final curl diameter. Matching the rod size to the desired curl pattern (tight spiral vs beach wave) ensures optimal disulfide bond reformation without frizzy over-processing.
formula_summary: Rod Color Chart: Red (4mm tight), Yellow (5mm), Blue (9mm standard), White (11mm full wave), Purple (14mm beach wave).

name: Keratin Treatment Dosage & Pass Guide
description: Calculate exact ounce/ml product application and flat iron temperature passes based on hair texture and damage level.
intro: Over-saturating keratin treatments leads to excessive smoke and wasted expensive product. This tool calculates exact fluid ounce requirements (1.5 oz fine to 3.0 oz thick/coarse) and iron heat passes.
formula_summary: Dosage: Short/Fine (30–45ml / 1–1.5oz), Medium (45–60ml / 1.5–2oz), Long/Coarse (60–90ml / 2–3oz). Temperature: 380°F–450°F.
keywords: how much keratin treatment to use

name: Lash Fan Weight & Safe-Load Calculator
description: Calculate mechanical fan weight (2D–10D) to match natural lash health and prevent follicle damage.
intro: Lash health is a science of volume geometry. A 5D fan of 0.05mm extensions exerts the identical mechanical load as a single 0.15mm classic extension. Calculate safe fan diameters to prevent traction alopecia on fine client lashes.
formula_summary: Safe Load Rule: 1D Classic (0.15mm) ≈ 3D (0.07mm) ≈ 5D (0.05mm) ≈ 10D Mega Volume (0.03mm ultra-fine).

name: Lash Mapping Blueprint Generator
description: Generate millimeter length maps (Cat Eye, Doll Eye, Squirrel, Natural) tailored to specific client eye shapes.
intro: Symmetrical lash sets require precise mapping. Choose your client's eye shape (Almond, Hooded, Deep Set, Round) and target style to generate an exact inner-to-outer corner millimeter transition map.
formula_summary: Map Rules: Inner corners must never exceed 7–8mm to prevent eyelid irritation. Peak length placed at outer third for Cat Eye, center for Doll Eye.

name: Lash Adhesive Humidity & Speed Adjuster
description: Adjust glue cure speed and drying time based on salon room temperature and relative humidity.
intro: Cyanoacrylate adhesive cures via moisture in the air. High humidity causes adhesive to set in 0.5s (causing shock polymerization), while low humidity slows drying time. Calculate adjustments for your salon humidity.
formula_summary: Humidity Physics: 45%–60% RH is ideal (1–2s cure). >70% RH requires slower glue; <40% RH requires glue booster / nebulizer.

name: Brow Tint & Developer Ratio Calculator
description: Calculate exact drop-to-cream ratios for 3% (10 Vol) oxidant and brow tint shades.
intro: Achieving consistent brow stains requires an exact 1:1 or 2:1 tint-to-developer ratio. This tool provides precise drop counts to eliminate runny mixes and uneven skin stains.
formula_summary: Brow Formula: 2cm tint cream = 10 drops of 3% (10 Vol) developer liquid (or 1:1 for cream oxidant).
keywords: how many drops developer brow tint

name: Brow Lamination Processing Timer
description: Determine Step 1 (Relaxing) and Step 2 (Neutralizing) timings based on hair thickness to prevent over-processing.
intro: Over-processing brow lamination breaks the hair's outer cuticle, resulting in frizzy, singed brow hairs. Calculate exact step-by-step processing times based on client hair thickness.
formula_summary: Step Timings: Fine brow hair (4–5 min Step 1), Medium hair (6–7 min Step 1), Coarse/Stubborn (8–10 min Step 1). Neutralize equal time.
keywords: how long to leave brow lamination

name: Acrylic Nail Monomer to Powder Ratio Guide
description: Calculate wet vs medium vs dry acrylic bead ratios for flawless structural apex bead placement.
intro: Incorrect monomer-to-powder ratios cause either brittle service breakdown (too dry) or contact dermatitis and lifting (too wet). Master bead consistency with this ratio guide.
formula_summary: Ideal Bead: 1.5:1 liquid-to-powder for medium bead. Surface should look satin-smooth within 3 seconds of picking up powder.

name: Gel Nail Cure Lamp Wattage & Time Calculator
description: Determine safe curing seconds based on UV/LED lamp wattage (24W, 48W, 54W) and gel opacity.
intro: Under-cured gel is a leading cause of HEMA allergies and premature chipping. Calculate exact cure times for base coats, builder gels, and opaque pigments based on your lamp specifications.
formula_summary: Cure Times: 48W/54W LED = 30s color, 60s builder gel. Traditional 36W UV = 120s full cure.
keywords: uv led lamp wattage cure time
how long to cure gel nails

name: Spray Tan DHA % & Development Calculator
description: Select DHA percentage (8%–14%) and rinse timers for Fitzpatrick skin types 1 through 6.
intro: DHA (Dihydroxyacetone) reacts with amino acids in the stratum corneum. Applying 14% DHA to a Fitzpatrick Type 1 skin type causes orange streaking. Calculate the exact DHA percentage and rinse time.
formula_summary: DHA Guidelines: Fitzpatrick 1–2 (8%–9% DHA), Fitzpatrick 3–4 (10%–12% DHA), Fitzpatrick 5–6 (14% DHA). Standard rinse: 8 hrs (or 2–4 hrs rapid).

options.text: Type 1: Very Fair / Burns Easily (8% DHA)

name: Chemical Peel Acid % & pH Strength Guide
description: Calculate free acid percentage based on concentration (20%–70%) and pH level for glycolic, salicylic, and lactic peels.
intro: In chemical exfoliation, pH is as critical as acid percentage. A 30% glycolic peel at pH 2.0 has far higher bioavailability than at pH 3.5. Estimate free acid value and neutralizing protocol.
formula_summary: Free Acid Formula: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation determines bioavailable active acid based on formula pKa and solution pH.

name: Booth Rent vs. Commission Profitability Calculator
description: Compare weekly service revenue, 50% commission splits, flat booth rent, and supply expenses to calculate net gains.
intro: Should you stay on a 50% commission split or rent your own private salon suite? Once you generate over $1,200/week in service sales, renting a booth ($250–$350/wk) typically yields an extra $1,500 to $3,000+ in monthly net profit.
formula_summary: Comparison Math: Commission Take-Home = Sales × Split % | Suite Take-Home = Sales - Flat Rent - Supply Cost. Monthly Diff = (Suite Net - Comm Net) × 4.33.

name: Hairdresser True Net Hourly Rate Calculator
description: Calculate real hourly earnings factoring in non-billable setup, sanitation, admin, and annual overhead expenses.
intro: Charging $80 for a 1-hour haircut does not mean you make $80/hour. Once you subtract rent, backbar supplies, taxes, and 10 hours of unpaid cleaning/admin per week, your true take-home rate might only be $32/hour. Discover your real hourly rate.
formula_summary: True Hourly Formula: (Annual Revenue - Annual Expenses) ÷ Total Working Hours (Chair Hours + Admin Hours × Weeks Worked).
keywords: how much should hair stylist charge

name: Salon Suite Startup Cost & Break-Even Estimator
description: Calculate security deposits, styling chair build-out, retail inventory, and client volume required to break even.
intro: Starting your own private salon suite requires upfront capital for security deposits, styling chairs, retail stock, and liability insurance. Calculate your total initial startup budget and exact client break-even point.
formula_summary: Break-Even Formula: Monthly Fixed Costs (Rent + Software + Insurance) ÷ Average Service Ticket = Clients Needed per Month.
keywords: how much to start a salon suite

name: Self-Employed Beauty Pro Tax & Tip Estimator
description: Estimate quarterly tax set-asides from card sales, cash tips, and write-off deductions.
intro: Independent beauty pros often get hit with unexpected tax bills. Use this estimator to calculate the exact 20%–30% quarterly tax set-aside from your service revenue and tip income.
formula_summary: Tax Estimation: Net Taxable Profit = Gross Sales + Tips - Deductible Supplies/Rent. Recommended Quarterly Set-Aside = 25%–30% of Net.
keywords: how much tax to save hairstylist

name: Retail Product Markup & Profit Margin Calculator
description: Calculate wholesale keystone markup (100%), profit per bottle, and monthly retail revenue goals.
intro: Retail sales are the highest-margin income in a salon suite. Using standard keystone markup (100%), selling just 2 bottles of shampoo per day adds $600 to $1,000+ in pure net monthly profit.
formula_summary: Keystone Formula: Retail Price = Wholesale Cost × 2.0 (100% markup). Profit Margin = 50%.

name: Salon Booking Software Fee Comparison
description: Compare monthly software subscriptions and credit card processing rates across Square, GlossGenius, Vagaro, and Fresha.
intro: Paying $40/month plus 2.9% + 30¢ in card fees adds up to thousands of dollars in hidden costs per year. Compare true annual costs across top solo booking platforms.
formula_summary: Annual Software Cost = (Monthly Fee × 12) + (Annual Card Volume × Card Processing Fee %).

name: Salon Net Profit Margin Calculator
description: Calculate overall net profit margins and identify expense leaks in rent, color inventory, and marketing.
intro: Healthy independent salon suites operate at 45% to 65% net profit margins. Calculate your overall business margin to ensure you aren't overspending on backbar stock.
formula_summary: Net Margin Formula: (Total Revenue - Total Overhead - Backbar Stock - Taxes) ÷ Total Revenue × 100.
keywords: how profitable is a salon suite

name: Fade & Clipper Guard Transition Guide
description: Visual guard transitions and lever adjustments (Open, Half, Closed) from skin (#00000) up to guard #8.
intro: A seamless blur fade requires systematic lever work. Transition cleanly between zero blade (0.5mm), guard #0.5 (1.5mm), guard #1 (3mm), and guard #1.5 (4.5mm) with this step-by-step guideline.
formula_summary: Guard Progression: Closed Blade (0.5mm) ➔ Open Blade (1.2mm) ➔ #0.5 Open (2.4mm) ➔ #1 Closed (3mm) ➔ #1.5 (4.5mm) ➔ #2 (6mm).

name: Beard Oil Carrier & Essential Oil Ratio Calculator
description: Formulate custom 30ml / 1oz beard oil recipes with exact carrier oil ratios (Jojoba, Argan) and 1% fragrance safety drops.
intro: Creating your own signature station beard oil? Formulate balanced carrier recipes (60% Jojoba, 30% Argan, 10% Castor) with a safe 1% essential oil scent load (6 drops per 30ml bottle).
formula_summary: Beard Oil Recipe (30ml / 1oz): 18ml Jojoba Oil + 9ml Argan Oil + 3ml Castor Oil + 6 Drops Essential Oils (1% fragrance load).

name: Hot Towel Shave Protocol & Steaming Timer
description: Optimal pre-shave oil absorption, steam towel temperature, and straight razor pass timings.
intro: The traditional straight razor hot towel service requires precise timing to soften coarse beard whiskers without causing razor burn. Follow the professional 5-step hot towel protocol.
formula_summary: Protocol: 2 min Pre-shave oil massage + 3 min Hot Towel (130°F/54°C) + First Pass with Grain + 2 min Second Towel + Against Grain Pass.

name: Essential Oil Dilution & Drop Calculator
description: Calculate exact safe essential oil drops for 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 3%, and 5% dilution in carrier oils (30ml, 60ml, 100ml).
intro: Essential oils are highly concentrated phytochemicals. Applying them undiluted can cause chemical sensitization. Calculate exact drop counts for facial massage (0.5%–1%), full body massage (2%), or acute pain relief (3%–5%).
formula_summary: Dilution Rules: 1 ml ≈ 20 drops. 1 fl oz (30ml) carrier @ 1% = 6 drops | @ 2% = 12 drops | @ 3% = 18 drops.

name: Massage Oil Coverage & Cost per Treatment
description: Estimate fluid ounce/ml usage per 60-min and 90-min session and calculate backbar oil cost per client.
intro: A standard 60-minute full body massage requires 20ml to 30ml (0.7 to 1.0 fl oz) of carrier oil. Calculate your exact backbar expense per treatment to ensure your pricing accounts for premium organic oils.
formula_summary: Cost Formula: (Carrier Volume Used × Cost/ml) + (Essential Drops × Cost/drop) = Backbar Expense per Client.

keywords: how much massage oil for 60 min

name: Hot Stone Temperature & Placement Guide
description: Safe water bath temperature standards (120°F–130°F / 49°C–54°C) and basalt stone placement map.
intro: Basalt hot stones retain thermal energy deep into muscular tissue. Maintaining proper water bath temperatures (120°F–130°F) prevents thermal burns while maximizing parasympathetic nervous system relaxation.
formula_summary: Thermal Safety: Water heater bath must be 120°F–130°F (49°C–54°C). Always test stones on therapist inner forearm before client placement.
